artworks.title: The Pleiades
artworks.description: Vedder's Metropolitan Museum canvas gathers Atlas' seven star-daughters — among them Celaeno, the Pleiad Poseidon loved, mother of Lycus and sometimes of Eurypylus. Not the harpy of the same name, nor the crimson bird.

artworks.title: The Dance of the Pleiades (Star Lore of All Ages, plate)
artworks.description: Olcott's 1911 star-lore plate reproduces Vedder's circling sisters — Celaeno among the Seven who mark the sailor's calendar.

artworks.title: Study for "The Pleiades"
artworks.description: Metropolitan Museum study for Vedder's Pleiades: Celaeno takes shape with her sisters in chalk and wash.

artworks.title: The Rising of the Pleiades (illustration to Hesiod)
artworks.description: Flaxman's outline for Hesiod's Works and Days: the rising of the Pleiades — Celaeno's cluster as the farmer's signal to harvest.

music.title: Atlàntida
music.description: Falla's scenic cantata after Verdaguer draws on Atlantis and the Pleiades' oceanic memory — Celaeno's star-sisterhood as Iberian mythic backdrop.

popCulture.title: Celaeno (Pleiad)
popCulture.description: One of the seven Pleiades; by Poseidon mother of Lycus — not the Danaid, not the harpy, not the cardinal.

popCulture.title: Pleiades (Greek mythology)
popCulture.description: The seven daughters of Atlas and Pleione — Celaeno among the sisters turned to stars.
